brief:
You are helping remake the classic JRPG "Final Fantasy" (NES, USA release, 1990).
Find fan resources on the public web that document what a faithful remake needs. Prefer sources with structured data (wiki tables, MediaWiki APIs, map atlases, FAQs with tables), and say which ones refuse automated clients if you know.

Asset types needed:
- world-map: World map (typical sources: map atlas (VGMaps, NESMaps); ROM map documentation)
- area-maps: Town, castle & dungeon maps (typical sources: map atlas (VGMaps); walkthrough maps)
- places: Places & regions (typical sources: fan wiki location lists)
- character-sprites: Playable classes & character sprites (typical sources: fan wiki job pages; sprite archives)
- npcs: NPCs (typical sources: fan wiki character list; walkthrough)
- enemies: Enemies & enemy sprites (typical sources: fan wiki bestiary; enemy FAQ)
- bosses: Bosses (typical sources: fan wiki boss pages; boss FAQ)
- formations: Encounter formations (typical sources: enemy formation tables; ROM data)
- weapons: Weapons (typical sources: fan wiki weapon tables)
- armor: Armor (typical sources: fan wiki armor tables)
- items: Items & key items (typical sources: fan wiki item tables)
- spells: Spells (typical sources: fan wiki magic pages; magic FAQ)
- shops: Shops & inns (typical sources: fan wiki town pages; shop lists)
- menus: Menu screens (menu type) (typical sources: fan wiki menu page; screenshots)
- rule-engine: Rule engine (formulas, stats, statuses, elements, levels) (typical sources: battle mechanics guides; fan wiki stat pages; disassembly notes)
- story: Story milestones & progression (typical sources: walkthroughs; fan wiki story section)
- music: Music themes (typical sources: soundtrack pages)

Already known (do not repeat): https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Final_Fantasy, https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Walkthrough:Final_Fantasy/Apoqliphoth, https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy/Gameplay, https://shrines.rpgclassics.com/nes/ff1/, https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Final_Fantasy, https://www.vgmaps.com/Atlas/NES/index.htm#F, https://archive.rpgamer.com/games/ff/ff1/ff1mid.html, https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/nes/522595-final-fantasy/faqs, https://www.spriters-resource.com/nes/ff/

Answer with JSON only: an array of objects
{"title": string, "url": "https://...", "assetTypes": [asset type ids], "kind": "wiki|map-atlas|walkthrough|faq|sprite-archive|rom-map|fan-site", "license": string, "notes": string}.
Use only real URLs you are confident exist. No commentary outside the JSON.

suggestions.title: NESMaps – Final Fantasy
suggestions.license: Fan-ripped maps; game assets © Square Enix; no explicit license
suggestions.notes: A ripped world map plus town, castle and dungeon maps. Some pages also note treasure locations. Static HTML with PNG images, so it scrapes easily.

suggestions.title: Mike's RPG Center – Final Fantasy
suggestions.license: Fan site, all rights reserved by author; game content © Square Enix
suggestions.notes: Clean HTML tables covering monsters (stats, gil, EXP), weapons, armor, items, magic, and shop inventories and prices by town. Encounters are listed by area, and there are dungeon maps and a walkthrough. Good for structured scraping.

suggestions.title: Final Fantasy Wiki (Fandom) MediaWiki API
suggestions.license: CC BY-SA 3.0 (text); images © Square Enix (fair use)
suggestions.notes: A MediaWiki API (action=parse / action=query) for the already-known wiki. Use it to pull wikitext tables instead of HTML. The HTML pages sit behind Cloudflare and often return 403 to automated clients without a browser-like UA. The API is more tolerant but rate-limited.

suggestions.title: Final Fantasy Wiki – Final Fantasy enemies
suggestions.notes: A bestiary index that links to individual enemy pages with infobox stats, weaknesses and sprites. Separate NES/PS/GBA/PSP stats are shown. Use the NES/original values.

suggestions.title: StrategyWiki – Final Fantasy
suggestions.notes: The guide root, with walkthrough chapters, a bestiary, equipment and magic subpages. The MediaWiki API is at https://strategywiki.org/w/api.php. It generally allows automated clients with a descriptive User-Agent.

suggestions.title: The Cutting Room Floor – Final Fantasy (NES)
suggestions.notes: Covers unused content, debug features and regional differences (Japan vs. USA). It also documents known bugs (e.g. ineffective spells, weapon crit bug) that a faithful USA remake must decide whether to reproduce.

suggestions.title: FF1 Randomizer (FiendsOfTheElements) source
suggestions.notes: C# code with ROM offsets and data structures for enemies, formations, shops, spells, equipment, maps and the battle engine. Its bug-fix flags list and explain vanilla mechanics bugs. Use the GitHub API or a raw clone.

suggestions.title: Final Fantasy Randomizer site
suggestions.notes: The randomizer's web frontend. Its flag descriptions summarize vanilla engine quirks. It is a JS app, so use the GitHub source above for data.

suggestions.title: Wikipedia – Final Fantasy (video game)
suggestions.notes: A high-level plot, development and soundtrack overview. The API is open to automated clients with a proper User-Agent.

suggestions.title: Zophar's Domain – Final Fantasy NSF
suggestions.license: Ripped game music © Square Enix; reference only
suggestions.notes: The NSF rip with a track list. Use it to identify themes and track order for reference. Do not redistribute the audio.

suggestions.title: VGMusic – NES MIDI archive
suggestions.notes: Fan MIDI transcriptions of Final Fantasy tracks (search the page for 'Final Fantasy'). They are useful as editable note data for re-orchestration.
